Old_Answer: Generally matter is always phase transitioning in both directions, at any temperature. For example, water even at room temperature will have molecules leaving the liquid state and joining the gaseous state, and other molecules leaving the gaseous state and joining the liquid state. At room temperature, it’s much more likely for a molecule to transition from gas to liquid than from liquid to gas, so you wind up with “most” of your molecules in liquid form. As you raise the temperature, you raise the chance of a liquid-to-gas transition and lower the chance of a gas-to-liqud transition, so the proportion of water in the liquid and gas states will adjust. At exactly the boiling point, the probability of a molecule transitioning is the same in either direction. So, these things are always happening. Stay safe and well! Of course, we’re talking about the vertical direction here - you could exert a force in some other direction. Under normal conditions, the up/down acceleration of gravity is g downward, and the sideways acceleration of gravity is zero. Question: What is the quantum field theory for someone just starting to learn it?
Old_Answer: It’s a lot of math that’s fairly hard to learn, for one thing. Conceptually it’s not that awful - the basic process you go through is that you know what your “initial conditions” are (the particles you have coming in toward a potential interaction). You then basically guess at possible final configurations (particles created, annihilated, etc., and how they are behaving), and then you can calculate the probability of the initial config leading to that final config. You repeat this process for more guessed final configs, until the total probability you have accounted for so far gets close enough to 1.0 to suit you. If it’s well below 1.0, then there’s some final configuration you haven’t considered yet. That’s basically it. The math takes care of enforcing conservation laws and all other physical requirements. The big difference between this and classical physics is that you do not “calculate” the final configuration - you “propose it” (guess at it) and then see how likely that is. I assume that with experience you get better and knowing what final configs to consider. Stay safe and well!
